title: GPU node-fleet sentinel: terraform module to orchestrate ASG + Karpenter in Private VPC
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create a Terraform module (private-vpc/gpu-fleet-sentinel) that provisions and manages GPU node fleets in Private VPCs with coordinated autoscaling between ASG (stable baseline) and Karpenter (burst scaler). The module must provide safe upgrade and health-check primitives, a sentinel reconciliation loop to maintain a minimum GPU capacity, and automated failover so customer inference SLOs are preserved during node upgrades or transient spot interruptions.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes inputs for instance_families, gpu_types, baseline_asg_capacity, karpenter_provisioner_config, node_labels, taints, and node_upgrade_strategy
Module deploys an ASG for reserved baseline capacity and a Karpenter provisioner for burst with correct IAM, subnets, and security groups in a Private VPC
Health-check daemon and preflight hooks are deployed: GPU driver daemonset version check, NVIDIA DCGM metrics, and node-ready probes with configurable grace periods
Sentinel controller (Terraform-managed k8s Job/Deployment) reconciles and re-creates baseline nodes if ASG drops below floor within configured timeout and emits events/metrics
Upgrade path tested: minor node AMI/driver update rollouts can drain nodes gracefully without violating token-latency SLO in staging
Observed metrics and alerts: per-node GPU-utilization, provisioning-latency, provisioning-failures, and baseline-capacity-fallback fire correctly in canary
Module has unit-level terraform tests (terratest) and CI pipeline gating on plan/apply to staging cluster
technical_notes: Design: two-layer capacity model: ASG = stable baseline (reserved instances), Karpenter = elastic burst. Use ASG Lifecycle hooks to coordinate graceful cordon/drain with node driver upgrades.
Terraform pieces: module creates ASG launch template, autoscaling group, policies, IAM roles, subnet attachments, and k8s terraform provider resources for Karpenter provisioner and DaemonSets.

Sentinel: lightweight controller implemented as k8s Deployment managed by the module (single container Go binary). Responsibilities: monitor ASG desired vs. actual capacity via AWS API, reconcile by annotating a maintenance CRD or bumping ASG if out of bounds, and emit Prometheus metrics.

Healthchecks: node-level readiness uses a driver-check sidecar + file-based probe; control-plane health uses synthetic inference requests routed to a test endpoint to measure tail latency during maintenance windows.

Node upgrades: implement 'drain-with-grace' workflow — set pod disruption budgets for inference pods, use preDrain hook that verifies driver and kernel compatibility, and fallback to Karpenter nodes if ASG drain reduces baseline below minimum.
Spot handling: Karpenter will prefer spot for burst; sentinel must detect elevated reclaim frequency and scale ASG temporarily to maintain SLOs.
Compatibility: module supports AMI updates, NVIDIA driver daemonset versioning, and quantized runtime libs. Provide inputs for custom nodeLabels and tolerations for mixed workloads.
Observability: export metrics on ASG shortfall, Karpenter provisioning latency, GPU driver ready ratio, and upgrade-failure-rate. Logs forwarded to cluster logging (fluentd) with structured tags.
Terraform state: recommend storing state in customer-managed S3 with encryption and locking via DynamoDB. Provide example backend config in README.
Secrets: no plaintext keys in module — use KMS-backed secrets for AMI IDs and HSM options. IAM least-privileges documented in README.

Why this approach: avoids large single-scaler coupling, gives deterministic baseline guarantees while allowing cost-efficient burst capacity (spot) via Karpenter. The sentinel provides safety nets for private deployments where capacity must be highly available.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module and run terraform plan against a disposable staging VPC (team infra account).
2) Deploy to staging cluster (canary) with baseline_asg_capacity=2 and karpenter_burst_limit=6. Run synthetic inference load for 24h.
3) Exercise node upgrade: bump driver daemonset to next patch, run rolling drain across ASG with sentinel enabled, verify no P50/P99 SLO regressions beyond threshold.
4) Run chaos test: simulate spot reclaim events and forced ASG termination; ensure sentinel increases ASG and Karpenter fills remaining demand as expected.
5) After 72h stable, promote module to preprod with baseline_asg_capacity=4 and run extended soak 7d with production-like workload.
6) Release to customers with migration guide and console toggles for dedicated baseline vs fully elastic mode.
test_plan: Unit: terratest suites for main module inputs, validate plan diffs for expected resources
Integration: terraform apply to staging cluster, validate Karpenter provisioner is created, ASG has expected tags and lifecycle hooks
E2E: run synthetic inference through local load generator; monitor GPU utilization and provisioning latency metrics
Chaos: run kube-monkey instance termination and AWS ASG instance termination tests to trigger sentinel fallback
Upgrade: simulate AMI and driver rollouts with controlled drain windows and check for errors in event logs and upgrade-failure-rate metrics
notes: 2026-02-20 decision: implement sentinel as a k8s-managed Deployment instead of external operator to simplify customer control-plane footprint.
2026-02-28 trade-off: using ASG lifecycle hooks adds AWS-specific complexity but gives deterministic baseline guarantees important for some enterprise customers.
2026-03-03 follow-up: add an opt-in feature to let Karpenter take the baseline role for non-enterprise customers to reduce cost.
Consideration: keep module small and composable; advanced policies (binpacking, topologySpread) are out of scope for MVP and will be provided via example configs.
